findings.claim: Signed favorable-minus-comparison contrasts at the observed selection nodes and over the complete observed window are strongest for the short pair-distance shells: pair_kernel_1.5 (endpoint_effects:9, integrated z 0.562, q 1.5e-4, positive batch fraction 1.0), pair_kernel_2.5 (endpoint_effects:10, z 0.631, q 2.2e-5, 1.0) and pair_kernel_3.5 (endpoint_effects:11, z 0.540, q 9.8e-5, 1.0), with pair_kernel_5.0 weaker (endpoint_effects:12, z 0.319, q 3.7e-3) and pair_kernel_7.0 reversed (endpoint_effects:13, z -0.485, q 1.5e-4, positive batch fraction 0.0). The same ordering appears in the branch-adjusted covariance contrasts (branch_adjusted:86, 87, 240, 241). These are selection-enrichment contrasts on a standardized coordinate feature, not an absolute geometric descriptor or a physical interaction energy.

Landmark soft-minimum and occupancy contrasts are mixed in sign across landmarks rather than a single shared direction: landmark_00_softmin is negative (endpoint_effects:14, z -0.481, q 8.1e-4) while landmark_00_occupancy3 is positive (endpoint_effects:15, z 0.545, q 2.4e-4); landmark_06_softmin is positive (endpoint_effects:32, z 0.294) while landmark_06_occupancy5 is negative (endpoint_effects:34, z -0.365); landmark_18_softmin is positive (endpoint_effects:68, z 0.264) while landmark_18_occupancy5 is negative (endpoint_effects:70, z -0.311). The survival-credit table shows the same sign heterogeneity (survival_effects:0, 70, 100, 186). Because soft-minimum distance and shell occupancy are different observables with different units, their signs cannot be compared as a shared quality axis.

Among shape components, shape_yy carries the strongest negative selection contrast (endpoint_effects:4, z -0.513, q 1.5e-5, positive batch fraction 0.0), with shape_xx (endpoint_effects:3, z -0.495) and shape_yz (endpoint_effects:8, z -0.212) also negative and shape_zz weaker (endpoint_effects:5, z -0.183). The branch-adjusted correlation for shape_yy is likewise negative (branch_adjusted:158, -0.103; branch_adjusted:235, -0.100). The regional local_cyy enrichment is negative at every landmark (regional_effects:5, 15, 75, 165, 195), so the shape_yy signal is not confined to one region.

Global centroid contrasts are weak and not batch-consistent: global_centroid_y is the only nominally significant component (endpoint_effects:1, z -0.243, q 0.014) with positive batch fraction 0.214, while global_centroid_x (endpoint_effects:0, z -0.111, q 0.257) and global_centroid_z (endpoint_effects:2, z -0.061, q 0.481) are not significant. After branch adjustment the centroid effects are further attenuated (branch_adjusted:77-79, 231-233). Centroid displacement is therefore not supported as a reproducible direction.

Joint-motion diagnostics are the most reproducible negative contrasts in the branch-adjusted table: joint_innovation_RMS_A (branch_adjusted:74, raw covariance; branch_adjusted:151, adjusted covariance; branch_adjusted:228 and 305, raw and adjusted correlation) and joint_internal_RMS_A (branch_adjusted:76, 153, 230, 307) are negative with same-sign batch fractions of 0.79-1.0 and q values down to 9.3e-5. joint_translation_RMS_A is weaker (branch_adjusted:75, 152, 229, 306). These are joint pose/shape diagnostics, not isolated marginal descriptors, and they are not physical interaction energies.

Within-selector joint diagnostics show that selection innovation is positively associated with native alignment (joint_diagnostics:1, mean 0.092, q 2.2e-9, positive batch fraction 1.0) and with teacher innovation-contrast alignment (joint_diagnostics:11, mean 0.226, q 2.2e-9, 1.0), while it is negatively associated with observed child score gain (joint_diagnostics:2, mean -0.036, q 1.8e-7, positive batch fraction 0.0). The teacher contrast is dominated by its internal fraction (joint_diagnostics:14, mean 0.787) rather than translation (joint_diagnostics:12) or rotation (joint_diagnostics:13), and atom participation is partial (joint_diagnostics:15, mean 0.384). These are descriptive within-selector associations with batch as the independent unit.

The information audit reports that the compressed-choice excess fixed-frame RMS is 0.081 A (CI 0.070-0.092) and that top-4 teacher overlap is 0.470 (CI 0.427-0.515), with compressed chosen teacher score correlation 0.102 (CI 0.065-0.140). The audit explicitly states this is not the full score-weighted reward or its FLOWR Jacobian and that nonnegative excess distance is by construction, not a causal affinity effect. Teacher contrast coherence (joint_diagnostics:4, mean 0.812), control root ESS (joint_diagnostics:5, mean 1.297) and sign calibration cosine (joint_diagnostics:10, mean 0.973) are descriptive and were not null-tested.

The observed-node linear fits over the complete observed window are not stationary: first-rate and last-rate z values have opposite signs for many features (e.g. continuous:0 landmark_00_soft_mass first_rate_z 9.27 vs last_rate_z -10.00; continuous:1 landmark_00_local_dx -17.49 vs 8.11; continuous:70 landmark_07_soft_mass 0.15 vs -5.58), and the curve-support audit records relative node RMSE of 0.30-0.99 with strong sign-conflict nodes for every audited feature. Polynomial fits were not accepted and extrapolation is not allowed. This is reported as supplied time variation; no time-conditioned reward information is proposed.

Turnover accounting separates population-contrast change from parent-child increment contrasts: for landmark_00_local_cxx the population rate is near zero (turnover:12) while the edge rate is negative (turnover:13, -4.34) and the turnover residual is positive (turnover:14, 4.29, q 0.038); for landmark_00_local_cyy the residual is positive (turnover:17, 5.05, q 0.033). Large positive residuals also appear at landmark_04_local_cxx (turnover:134, 5.67), landmark_07_local_cxx (turnover:224, 5.08), landmark_07_local_cyy (turnover:227, 5.63), landmark_08_local_cxx (turnover:254, 5.54), landmark_08_local_cyy (turnover:257, 4.58), landmark_16_local_cyy (turnover:497, 6.37), landmark_17_local_cxx (turnover:524, 5.24), landmark_17_local_cyy (turnover:527, 4.51), landmark_19_local_cxx (turnover:584, 5.30) and landmark_19_local_cyy (turnover:587, 5.37). The residual is an accounting diagnostic that includes score reclassification and extant-parent weighting, not a causal selection effect or atom velocity.

Descendant credit is recorded joint-head credit, not decoded terminal affinity: decoded_terminal_learning_labels_available is false, the label semantics are recorded affinities removed with an equal score prior, and the lineage support table states multiple testing was BH jointly over 400 survival field/measure tests and is not terminal affinity effects. The lineage table also records 349 nodes with fewer than 3 ancestors and 531 with fewer than 6, so ancestral coverage is thin for many nodes. Last-record credit therefore cannot be presented as final affinity benefit, and the unavailable terminal comparison is reported as unavailable.

Multiplicity-adjusted support changes the ranking relative to point estimates: in the raw-covariance branch-adjusted block, pair_kernel_2.5 has the smallest q (branch_adjusted:10, q 0.116) and pair_kernel_1.5 the next (branch_adjusted:9, q 0.134), while shape_yy (branch_adjusted:4, q 0.153) and shape_yz (branch_adjusted:8, q 0.131) have larger point estimates in some cases but do not survive the same multiplicity adjustment. Several features with nonzero point estimates (e.g. branch_adjusted:0, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 11, 12, 13) have q above 0.2. A priority decision based on q rather than point estimate alone would therefore favor the short pair kernels over the shape components.

Independent-batch agreement and opposing observations constrain the coordinate rules: shape_yy has same-sign batch fraction 1.0 in both raw and adjusted correlation (branch_adjusted:158, 235) and pair_kernel_1.5/2.5 have 0.86-0.93 (branch_adjusted:163, 164, 240, 241), whereas global_centroid_y has positive batch fraction 0.214 (endpoint_effects:1) and pair_kernel_7.0 has 0.0 (endpoint_effects:13). A counterexample that would weaken the short-pair-kernel direction is a batch in which the pair_kernel_1.5 or 2.5 contrast reverses sign; the supplied same-sign fractions show this occurs in roughly 1 of 14 batches for the short kernels and in all batches for pair_kernel_7.0, so the short-kernel direction is used with that reproducibility caveat.

hypotheses.claim: Hypothesis: a coordinate intervention that increases the short pair-distance shell density (pair_kernel_1.5 and pair_kernel_2.5) at the observed selection nodes over the complete observed window will raise the favorable-minus-comparison contrast, with the intended response measured as a signed change in those shell contrasts and the target origin being the supplied pair-shell coordinate. Discriminating failure: a batch in which the pair_kernel_1.5 or 2.5 contrast reverses sign.

Hypothesis: reducing the shape_yy component and the regional local_cyy enrichment at the supplied landmarks will raise the favorable-minus-comparison contrast, with the intended response measured as a signed change in shape_yy and local_cyy and the target origin being the supplied landmark coordinates. Discriminating failure: a batch in which the shape_yy or local_cyy contrast becomes positive.

Hypothesis: reducing joint innovation and internal RMS while retaining freedom in the surrounding coordinates will raise the favorable-minus-comparison contrast, with the intended response measured as a signed change in the joint RMS diagnostics and the target origin being the joint pose/shape coordinates. Discriminating failure: a batch in which the joint RMS contrast becomes positive.

Hypothesis: the large positive turnover residuals at the local_cxx and local_cyy components of landmarks 04, 07, 08, 16, 17 and 19 reflect changing cohort composition and parent weighting rather than within-path change, and a coordinate intervention targeting those components would be confounded by reclassification. Discriminating failure: a batch in which the population rate and the edge rate have the same sign and similar magnitude, leaving no residual.

Hypothesis: the observed first-rate and last-rate sign reversals for the landmark soft-mass and local displacement features indicate non-stationary within-window behavior, so a stationary whole-window rule would be mis-specified for those features. Discriminating failure: a feature whose first-rate and last-rate z values have the same sign and whose curve-support audit shows no strong sign-conflict nodes.

Hypothesis: selection innovation that is positively aligned with native alignment and teacher innovation contrast but negatively associated with observed child score gain indicates that the selector favors internal teacher-contrast alignment over immediate child score improvement. Discriminating failure: a batch in which the innovation-child-score-gain association becomes positive.

limitations: Descendant credit is recorded joint-head credit, not decoded terminal affinity; decoded_terminal_learning_labels_available is false and the unavailable terminal comparison is reported as unavailable.
Turnover residual includes score reclassification and extant-parent weighting, not only resampling, and is an accounting diagnostic rather than a causal selection effect or atom velocity.
Adjusted branch covariance is supplied evidence; region moments themselves are not rigid-motion residuals, and no adjustment beyond the supplied tool is claimed.
Curve fitting does not establish causal benefit or a gradient; no time bins or outside-window analysis are available.
Static teachers are last-learning-node forecasts, not actual final structures.
All weak and null scalar effects are retained; current study outcomes are withheld from design roles.
The executing pointcloud scalar has no pair-kernel, moment, joint-motif or geometry-block term, so pair-kernel and moment findings remain diagnostic and descriptive.
Temperatures are immutable task parameters and no temperature edit is proposed.
